Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

We present results from STAR on 3-particle azimuthal correlations for a $3<p_T<4$ GeV/c trigger particle with two softer $1<p_T<2$ GeV/c particles. Results are shown for pp, d+Au and high statistics Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200 GeV$. We observe a 3-particle correlation in central Au+Au collisions which may indicate the presence of conical emission. In addition, the dependence of the observed signal angular position on the $p_T$ of the associated particles can be used to distinguish conical flow from simple QCD-\v{C}erenkov radiation. An important aspect of the analysis is the subtraction of combinatorial backgrounds. Systematic uncertainties due to this subtraction and the flow harmonics $v_2$ and $v_4$ are investigated in detail.

outputs.L1: We present STAR results on three-particle azimuthal correlations involving a trigger particle with \(3 < p_T < 4\) GeV/\(c\) and two softer associated particles with \(1 < p_T < 2\) GeV/\(c\). Results are reported for \(p+p\), \(d+\)Au, and high-statistics Au+Au collisions at \(\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 200\) GeV. In central Au+Au collisions, we observe a three-particle correlation that may indicate the presence of conical emission. Furthermore, the dependence of the signal’s angular position on the \(p_T\) of the associated particles can be used to distinguish conical flow from simple QCD-\v{C}erenkov radiation. A key aspect of the analysis is the subtraction of combinatorial backgrounds. Systematic uncertainties arising from this subtraction and from the flow harmonics \(v_2\) and \(v_4\) are investigated in detail.
outputs.L2: We report STAR measurements of three-particle azimuthal correlations using a trigger particle with \(3<p_T<4\) GeV/\(c\) and two lower-momentum associated particles with \(1<p_T<2\) GeV/\(c\). The data include \(pp\), \(d+\)Au, and high-statistics Au+Au collisions at \(\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200\) GeV. In central Au+Au events, a three-particle correlation is detected that could signal conical emission. Furthermore, studying how the angular location of this structure varies with the transverse momentum of the associated particles may differentiate conical flow from conventional QCD-\(\check{\mathrm{C}}\)erenkov radiation. A central element of the analysis is the removal of combinatorial background contributions. The systematic uncertainties associated with this procedure, as well as with the flow coefficients \(v_2\) and \(v_4\), are examined thoroughly.

The STAR experiment measured three-particle azimuthal correlations using trigger particles with transverse momenta of \(3<p_T<4\) GeV/\(c\) and two associated particles in the range \(1<p_T<2\) GeV/\(c\). The analysis covered \(pp\), \(d+\)Au, and high-statistics Au+Au collisions at a center-of-mass energy per nucleon pair of \(\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200\) GeV.

In central Au+Au collisions, STAR observed a three-particle correlation structure that may be consistent with conical emission associated with the interaction of a high-energy parton and the dense medium. Measuring how the angular position of this structure varies with the transverse momentum of the associated particles could help distinguish medium-induced conical flow from simple QCD-Čerenkov radiation, as the two mechanisms are expected to exhibit different momentum dependences.

Because such correlation measurements are sensitive to the large underlying event in heavy-ion collisions, the analysis gives particular attention to the subtraction of combinatorial backgrounds. It also systematically evaluates uncertainties arising from the elliptic- and fourth-order flow harmonics, \(v_2\) and \(v_4\), which can significantly influence the extracted three-particle correlation signal.
outputs.L4:
The STAR experiment measured three-particle azimuthal correlations in proton–proton, deuteron–gold, and gold–gold collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 200 GeV per nucleon pair. Events were selected by requiring a high-transverse-momentum trigger particle with \(3<p_T^{\rm trig}<4\) GeV/\(c\), together with two associated particles having \(1<p_T^{\rm assoc}<2\) GeV/\(c\). The correlations were studied as functions of the azimuthal-angle differences \(\Delta\phi_1\) and \(\Delta\phi_2\) between each associated particle and the trigger.

To isolate genuine jet-related three-particle structures, large combinatorial backgrounds had to be removed. These included events in which one associated particle was correlated with the trigger while the other came from the underlying event, as well as backgrounds in which neither associated particle belonged to the trigger jet. Contributions from collective anisotropic flow were incorporated using measured elliptic- and fourth-harmonic-flow coefficients. The normalization of the background and uncertainties associated with the flow treatment, event mixing, and assumptions about the signal were varied to estimate the systematic uncertainty.

The correlation patterns in \(p+p\) and \(d+\)Au collisions are dominated by structures expected from ordinary jet fragmentation: a near-side peak around \((\Delta\phi_1,\Delta\phi_2)=(0,0)\) and an away-side enhancement near \((\pi,\pi)\). In peripheral Au+Au collisions, the correlations remain broadly similar. In central Au+Au collisions, however, the away-side distribution develops a more complex shape. In addition to strength along the diagonal, where both associated particles are emitted on the same side of the away-side jet axis, significant off-diagonal peaks appear near \((\pi+\theta,\pi-\theta)\) and \((\pi-\theta,\pi+\theta)\). Such off-diagonal structures are difficult to explain solely through broadening or deflection of a single recoil jet, because those mechanisms tend to populate the diagonal.

The observed pattern is consistent with conical emission induced by the interaction of the away-side parton with the dense medium produced in central Au+Au collisions. Possible mechanisms include a hydrodynamic Mach cone generated by energy deposition in the medium and QCD-Čerenkov gluon radiation. These scenarios make different qualitative predictions for the cone angle. A Mach-cone angle should be governed mainly by the medium’s speed of sound and therefore depend only weakly on the momentum of the associated particles. In contrast, the characteristic angle from Čerenkov-like radiation is generally expected to decrease as the associated-particle momentum increases.

Consequently, measuring the position of the off-diagonal peaks in several associated-\(p_T\) intervals provides a means of distinguishing between the proposed mechanisms. Within the available precision, the central Au+Au data exhibit a cone-like away-side correlation whose angular scale shows no strong momentum dependence, favoring an interpretation based on conical collective response over a simple QCD-Čerenkov-radiation picture. Higher-statistics measurements and tighter constraints on flow-related backgrounds are nevertheless required for a definitive identification of the underlying mechanism.
outputs.L5:
The STAR experiment at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider studies collisions between heavy ions and protons at energies ranging from a few GeV to several hundred GeV. Its large detector system allows researchers to track thousands of particles produced in each collision and investigate the properties of strongly interacting matter.

Results from STAR have provided important evidence for the formation of the quark–gluon plasma, a state in which quarks and gluons are no longer confined inside individual protons and neutrons. Measurements of particle flow, jet energy loss, and the production of strange and heavy-flavor particles have helped scientists characterize this extremely hot and dense medium. STAR’s energy-scan program also compares results at different collision energies, expressed in GeV, to search for changes in the behavior of nuclear matter and possible features of the quantum chromodynamics phase diagram.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a concise abstract for a STAR study of three-particle azimuthal correlations in pp, d+Au, and Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200$ GeV, emphasizing possible conical emission and background-subtraction uncertainties.
counterfactuals.output: Three-particle azimuthal correlations of a high-\(p_T\) trigger hadron with two associated hadrons are studied in \(p+p\), \(d+\)Au, and Au+Au collisions at \(\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200\) GeV with the STAR detector. In central Au+Au collisions, the away-side correlation exhibits off-diagonal structures consistent with associated particles emitted at similar angles on opposite sides of \(\Delta\phi=\pi\), as expected from conical emission induced by jet–medium interactions. These features are not prominent in the \(p+p\) and \(d+\)Au reference data. Quantitative interpretation is limited by uncertainties in subtracting combinatorial and trigger-correlated backgrounds, including elliptic- and higher-order flow contributions and the normalization assumptions used in the subtraction. The results therefore suggest, but do not uniquely establish, conical emission in the hot medium.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize STAR results for a $3<p_T<4$ GeV/c trigger particle correlated with two $1<p_T<2$ GeV/c associated particles, including the collision systems, interpretation of the central Au+Au signal, and systematic effects from $v_2$ and $v_4$.
counterfactuals.output:
STAR measured three-particle azimuthal correlations at \(\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200\) GeV using a \(3<p_T^{\rm trig}<4\) GeV/\(c\) trigger and two \(1<p_T^{\rm assoc}<2\) GeV/\(c\) particles in \(p+p\), \(d+\)Au, and peripheral-to-central Au+Au collisions.

- In \(p+p\), \(d+\)Au, and peripheral Au+Au, the correlation is dominated by ordinary jet-like peaks: near-side \((0,0)\) and away-side \((\pi,\pi)\).
- In central Au+Au, additional away-side off-diagonal peaks appear near  
  \[
  (\Delta\phi_1,\Delta\phi_2)\approx(\pi\pm1.4,\;\pi\mp1.4).
  \]
  These correspond to two associated particles emitted on opposite sides of the recoil direction and were interpreted as evidence for cone-like medium response to the quenched away-side parton—consistent with Mach-cone shock emission or another conical-radiation mechanism. The extracted cone angle was about \(1.37\) rad and showed little associated-\(p_T\) dependence. The result establishes conical emission phenomenologically but does not by itself uniquely identify the microscopic mechanism.

The dominant systematic uncertainty comes from subtracting the elliptic-flow background, \(v_2\). Varying \(v_2\) within estimates based on different flow methods changes the overall yields and especially diagonal structures. The \(v_4\) term, usually constrained relative to \(v_2^2\), adds a smaller fourfold modulation and can alter both diagonal and off-diagonal amplitudes. Nevertheless, under the tested \(v_2\) and \(v_4\) variations, the central-Au+Au off-diagonal peak positions and qualitative cone-like structure remain robust.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a conference-proceedings abstract on using three-particle correlations to distinguish conical flow from QCD-\v{C}erenkov radiation in high-energy nuclear collisions.
counterfactuals.output:
**Three-Particle Correlations as a Discriminator of Conical Flow and QCD-Čerenkov Radiation in Nuclear Collisions**

Away-side double-peak structures in dihadron azimuthal correlations have been interpreted as signatures of either hydrodynamic conical flow induced by jet-energy deposition or QCD-Čerenkov gluon radiation. We investigate how these mechanisms can be distinguished using three-particle correlations in high-energy nucleus–nucleus collisions. Correlating a high-\(p_T\) trigger particle with two lower-\(p_T\) associated particles exposes the two-dimensional away-side topology, separating genuine conical emission—characterized by off-diagonal peaks—from broadened or deflected jet fragmentation. The decisive observable is the dependence of the extracted cone angle and peak widths on associated-particle momentum, collision centrality, and orientation relative to the event plane. Hydrodynamic Mach-cone scenarios predict an approximately momentum-independent angle governed primarily by the medium-averaged speed of sound, together with collective-flow and path-length effects. In contrast, QCD-Čerenkov radiation generically produces a dispersive angle determined by the gluon-energy dependence of the medium’s chromorefractive index. We outline a cumulant-based analysis incorporating mixed-event acceptance corrections and subtraction of anisotropic-flow backgrounds, including event-by-event flow fluctuations. Model comparisons demonstrate that differential three-particle measurements can constrain the angular dispersion and medium response more strongly than two-particle correlations alone. These observables provide a practical framework for distinguishing hydrodynamic conical flow from coherent QCD-Čerenkov radiation and for quantifying the coupling of energetic partons to the quark–gluon plasma.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe the main findings and analysis challenges of STAR’s three-particle azimuthal-correlation measurement at RHIC, with particular attention to combinatorial-background subtraction and flow harmonics.
counterfactuals.output:
STAR used a high-\(p_T\) trigger hadron and two lower-\(p_T\) associated hadrons, plotting the yield versus  
\[
\Delta\phi_1=\phi_1-\phi_{\rm trig},\qquad
\Delta\phi_2=\phi_2-\phi_{\rm trig}.
\]

### Main observations

- In \(p+p\), \(d+\)Au, and peripheral Au+Au, the away side was concentrated near \((\pi,\pi)\), as expected from ordinary back-to-back jet fragmentation.
- In central Au+Au, the away-side three-particle correlation broadened and developed structures displaced from \(\pi\).
- Particularly important were **off-diagonal peaks** near
  \[
  (\Delta\phi_1,\Delta\phi_2)\simeq(\pi+\theta,\pi-\theta)
  \]
  and the reflected point, with \(\theta\sim1.3\)–\(1.4\) rad. Such pairs place the two associated particles on opposite sides of the recoil direction and were interpreted as evidence for cone-like emission.
- The extracted cone angle was approximately independent of centrality and associated-particle momentum within uncertainties. This was viewed as qualitatively compatible with a medium-response or Mach-cone picture and less natural for simple deflected-jet fragmentation or momentum-dependent Cherenkov-radiation scenarios.
- Diagonal strength, where both particles appear on the same side of the recoil axis, was less distinctive because it can also arise from jet broadening, deflection, \(k_T\), and ordinary fragmentation.

Thus, the historically important result was not merely the away-side double peak in a two-particle correlation, but the apparent off-diagonal three-particle structure. Nevertheless, it did not uniquely establish a Mach shock.

### Combinatorial-background problem

The genuine jet-related triplet yield is small compared with the number of random trigger–associate–associate combinations. STAR therefore separated the background into two broad classes:

1. **Hard–soft background:** one associated particle is genuinely correlated with the trigger, while the second is combinatorial. It was constructed from the measured trigger-associated two-particle correlation combined with mixed-event particles.

2. **Soft–soft background:** neither associated particle is correlated with the trigger, although the two associated particles can be correlated with each other through flow, minijets, resonance decays, or other inclusive-event physics. Minimum-bias event mixing and multiplicity corrections were used to model this component.

Normalization was tied to two-particle zero-yield-at-minimum or zero-yield-at-one assumptions and to corrections for non-Poisson multiplicity fluctuations. This is a major sensitivity: because the raw combinatorial background is much larger than the residual signal, a small error in its normalization or shape can produce or erase apparent peaks. Trigger-induced multiplicity biases and differences between triggered and inclusive event samples add further uncertainty.

### Role of flow harmonics

The mixed-event background cannot be taken as azimuthally flat. It must be modulated by collective flow. The subtraction included terms generated by products such as

\[
v_2^{\rm trig}v_2^{\rm assoc}\cos(2\Delta\phi)
\]

and analogous \(v_4\) terms, as well as associate–associate and mixed three-particle harmonic terms. STAR generally bracketed \(v_2\) using different measurements, such as event-plane and multi-particle-cumulant estimates, and parameterized \(v_4\) relative to \(v_2^2\). The uncertainty in \(v_2\) was among the dominant systematic errors because residual elliptic flow naturally produces strong diagonal and away-side curvature.

A key later caveat is that the original analyses were performed before event-by-event odd harmonics—especially triangular flow \(v_3\)—were fully appreciated. Fluctuation-driven \(v_3\) can create an away-side double-hump in two-particle correlations and nontrivial structures in three-particle maps. If only \(v_2\) and \(v_4\) are subtracted, part of what remains can be attributed to unremoved higher-harmonic collective flow rather than conical jet-induced emission.

In summary, STAR found a robust-looking, centrality-dependent off-diagonal away-side structure that was suggestive of conical medium response. Its quantitative interpretation, however, was limited by the enormous combinatorial background, normalization assumptions, flow uncertainties and fluctuations, and—most importantly in hindsight—the incomplete treatment of higher harmonics such as \(v_3\).
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Produce a brief scientific overview of evidence for conical emission in central Au+Au collisions from high-statistics STAR data, comparing the results with pp and d+Au reference measurements.
counterfactuals.output:
High-statistics STAR measurements at \(\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200\) GeV used three-particle azimuthal correlations with a high-\(p_T\) trigger hadron and two lower-\(p_T\) associated hadrons. After subtracting combinatorial and elliptic-flow backgrounds, central Au+Au collisions showed a distinctive away-side structure: besides correlations along the diagonal \((\Delta\phi_1\!\approx\!\Delta\phi_2)\), significant off-diagonal peaks appeared near  
\[
(\Delta\phi_1,\Delta\phi_2)\approx(\pi+\theta,\pi-\theta),
\]
with \(\theta\approx1.37\) rad and little dependence on associated-particle \(p_T\).

These off-diagonal correlations indicate that two particles can be emitted on opposite sides of a cone around the recoil-jet direction. Such a pattern is difficult to generate through simple jet broadening or deflection, which predominantly produces diagonal correlations. In pp and d+Au reference data, STAR instead observed the expected narrow near- and away-side jet peaks, with no comparable off-diagonal cone-like signal. The enhancement therefore appears specific to the hot, dense medium formed in central Au+Au collisions.

The result was interpreted as evidence consistent with medium-induced conical emission—such as a Mach-cone response to jet energy loss—rather than ordinary vacuum jet fragmentation or cold-nuclear-matter effects. It remains an indication rather than unique proof, because the extraction depends on flow-background modeling and later work showed that event-by-event higher-order flow harmonics can also generate broad or double-peaked away-side structures.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
